R7AF-bear-walk-0002.name: 1.3 km S of Captain Creek
R7AF-bear-walk-0002.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R7AF-bear-walk-0002.parkWhat: pull off on Otter Road FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2020 (6 years old), 260 m S: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2017 (fire G11636), 380 m SE: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SW facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 100 m NE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from District of Tumbler Ridge, about 102 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 54.31531, -121.64011, pull off on Otter Road FSR (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 1.2 km NE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 393 m, about 63 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-16, Region 7A. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-05, closures 2026-10-16.
R7AF-bear-walk-0002.popWhy: Popular (more hunters): MU 7-16: about 1,268 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.34 days per square km, top third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

R7AF-duck-backcountry-0002.name: Unnamed wetland by Parsnip River
R7AF-duck-backcountry-0002.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R7AF-duck-backcountry-0002.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: About 29 wetlands within 2 km (estimate): ducks move between them.
Beside Parsnip River: backwater or oxbow (estimate).
Elevation 757 m: under 900 m, open water later in fall.

seasonRows.notes: District 7. Within the 8 a day: 4 northern pintails, 4 canvasbacks, 2 Barrow's or common goldeneyes together, 2 harlequins. Possession 24: 12, 12, 6, 6.

plan: Drive: from District of Tumbler Ridge, about 83 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 54.46264, -121.66997, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 6.2 km NE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 206 m, about 144 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 120 m NE of the spot at 757 m (54.48958, -121.58484). Water: unnamed wetland right here (estimate).
Hunt: ducks, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Set up on the shore with the wind at your back: ducks land into the wind (Tip). Shoot only birds you can retrieve.
Use: 12 gauge, steel 2 to 4 (non toxic shot only), modified or improved cylinder rated for steel, plugged to 3 shells (regs).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-23, Region 7A. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-05, closures 2026-10-16.
